The '''Chiefs–Raiders rivalry''' is a [[National Football League]] (NFL) [[List of NFL rivalries|rivalry]] between the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] and [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gay |first=Nancy |date=2006-12-15 |title=Hunt-Davis rivalry was built on respect |url=https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/Hunt-Davis-rivalry-was-built-on-respect-2542987.php |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=SFGATE |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 12, 2014 |title=Born of Disrespect, Chiefs-Raiders Rivalry Runs Deep |url=https://www.chiefs.com/news/born-of-disrespect-chiefs-raiders-rivalry-runs-deep-14566763 |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=Kansas City Chiefs |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Football |first=The Chancellor of |date=2011-06-04 |title=The AFL: A True American Success Story |url=https://taylorblitztimes.com/2011/06/03/the-afl-a-true-american-success-story/ |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=Taylor Blitz Times |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=TheTorch |first=Honor Warren Wells |date=June 7, 2018 |title=Oakland Raiders and Kansas City Chiefs: A Historic Rivalry, a Hot Encounter |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/401413-oakland-raiders-and-kansas-city-chiefs-historic-rivalry-a-hot-encounter |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2017 |title=A History Of The Raiders And Chiefs Rivalry Through The Years |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/a-history-of-the-raiders-and-chiefs-rivalry-through-the-years-19942798 |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=Las Vegas Raiders |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Eno |first=Greg |date=2010-02-06 |title=Forty Years Ago, the AFL Showed the NFL Who the Real Fools Were |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/340685-forty-years-ago-the-afl-showed-the-nfl-who-the-real-fools-were |access-date=2022-07-20 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kerhoff |first=Blair |date=2016-12-07 |title=There are many reasons for the hatred between the Chiefs and Raiders, here are five |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article119520873.html |website=The Wichita Eagle}}</ref>

The rivalry between the Chiefs and Raiders is considered to be one of the NFL's most bitter rivalries.<ref name="Top 10">{{cite magazine|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/multimedia/photo_gallery/2005/12/15/gallery.oldrivals/content.8.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051217181115/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/multimedia/photo_gallery/2005/12/15/gallery.oldrivals/content.8.html|archive-date=December 17, 2005|title=Top 10 NFL Rivalries of All Time|magazine=Sports Illustrated|publisher=si.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |author=Ehrlich |first=Matthew C. |title=Kansas City vs. Oakland: The Bitter Sports Rivalry That Defined an Era |date=15 August 2019 |publisher=University of Illinois Press |isbn=978-0-252-05150-0 |oclc=1155496074}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Mike |date=2020-11-23 |title=The Bitter Chiefs and Raiders Rivalry Sparked Hatred, Rule Change |url=https://www.sportscasting.com/the-bitter-chiefs-and-raiders-rivalry-sparked-hatred-rule-change/ |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=Sportscasting {{!}} Pure Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Brown">{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Ramone |date=September 19, 2009 |title=Oakland Raiders and Kansas City Chiefs Rivalry and Connections |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/257977-raiders-and-chiefs-rivalry-and-connections |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> Since the [[American Football League]] (AFL) was established in [[1960 American Football League season|1960]], the Chiefs and Raiders have shared the same division, first being the AFL Western Conference, and since the [[AFL–NFL merger]] in {{nfly|1970}}, the [[AFC West]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2000-12-01 |title=Raiders, Chiefs go way back: Ex-AFL rivals meet Sunday for 80th time in regular season |url=http://www.profootballhof.com/history/mainpage.cfm?cont_id=29914 |archive-date=December 1, 2000 |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=Pro Football Hame of Fame|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20001201232400/http://www.profootballhof.com/history/mainpage.cfm?cont_id=29914 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Moss |first=Matt |date=October 11, 2000 |title=Flashback: Wild, wild west: A new century shootout sunk the Chiefs |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/001010flashback.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20001204214200/http://www.nfl.com/news/001010flashback.html |archive-date=2000-12-04 |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=NFL}}</ref>

The Chiefs lead the overall series, 77–56–2. The two teams have met three times in the [[National Football League playoffs|playoffs]], with the Chiefs holding a 2–1 record.<ref name="Head2Head"/>

==History==
The teams first met in [[1960 American Football League season|1960]] when the Chiefs were known as the Dallas Texans. The Texans defeated the Raiders 34–16 in the team's first game at [[Kezar Stadium|Oakland]],<ref name="Football Database">{{cite web|url=http://www.footballdb.com/teamvsteam.html?tm=16&opp=23|title=Kansas City Chiefs vs. Oakland Raiders All Time Results|publisher=The Football Database}}</ref><ref name="1960 Dallas Texans">{{cite web|url=http://profootballreference.com/teams/kan1960.htm|title=1960 Dallas Texans Statistics & Players - Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=August 29, 2016}}</ref><ref name="1960 Oakland Raiders">{{cite web|url=http://profootballreference.com/teams/rai1960.htm|title=1960 Oakland Raiders Statistics & Players - Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=August 29, 2016|archive-date=May 8, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060508211327/http://www.profootballreference.com/teams/rai1960.htm}}</ref> then the Raiders defeated the Texans 20–19 at [[Cotton Bowl (stadium)|Dallas]].<ref name="1960 Dallas Texans"/><ref name="1960 Oakland Raiders"/>

The rivalry did not become so apparent until the [[Kansas City Athletics]] [[Major League Baseball|baseball]] team moved to [[Oakland, California]], in [[1968 in baseball|1968]]. In [[1969 in baseball|1969]], the [[Kansas City Royals]] expansion team was placed in the same division as the Athletics. The [[1966 Kansas City Chiefs season|1966 Chiefs team]] participated in the first [[Super Bowl I|AFL-NFL World Championship Game]], later known as the [[Super Bowl]]. The Chiefs and Raiders had identical 12–2 records in 1968 and faced off in a playoff game to decide who would go to face the [[New York Jets]] for the [[AFL Championship]]. The Raiders won, 41–6.

[[File:1986 Jeno's Pizza - 49 - Robert Holmes.jpg|thumb|190px|left|The Raiders playing the Chiefs in the 1969 [[1969 American Football League Championship Game|AFL championship game]]]]
The following year, in [[1969 American Football League season|1969]], the Raiders beat the Chiefs twice in the regular season<ref name="1969 Kansas City Chiefs">{{cite web|url=http://profootballreference.com/teams/kan1969.htm|title=1969 Kansas City Chiefs Statistics & Players - Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=August 29, 2016|archive-date=March 17, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060317151403/http://www.profootballreference.com/teams/kan1969.htm}}</ref><ref name="1969 Oakland Raiders">{{cite web|url=http://profootballreference.com/teams/rai1969.htm|title=1969 Oakland Raiders Statistics & Players - Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=August 29, 2016|archive-date=March 17, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060317142705/http://www.profootballreference.com/teams/rai1969.htm}}</ref> and went on to win the AFL Western Conference title. The teams met in the 1969 AFL Championship Game at Oakland and the underdog Chiefs won 17–7.<ref name="1969 Kansas City Chiefs"/><ref name="1969 Oakland Raiders"/> The Chiefs participated in [[Super Bowl IV]] a week later and defeated the NFL's [[spread betting|heavily favored]] [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref name="1969 Kansas City Chiefs"/> It was not until [[1976 NFL season|1976]] that Oakland won their [[Super Bowl XI|first Super Bowl championship]].<ref name="1976 Oakland Raiders">{{cite web|url=http://profootballreference.com/teams/rai1976.htm|title=1976 Oakland Raiders Statistics & Players - Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=August 29, 2016|archive-date=March 17, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060317151620/http://www.profootballreference.com/teams/rai1976.htm}}</ref>

In the first meeting between the teams during the [[1970 NFL season]]—both teams' first in the newly merged NFL—the Chiefs held a 17–14 lead late in the fourth quarter and appeared ready to run out the clock. Chiefs quarterback Len Dawson rolled right and gained enough yardage for a first down, and as he fell to the ground, Raiders defensive end [[Ben Davidson]] dove into Dawson with his helmet; in retaliation, Davidson was attacked by Chiefs wide receiver Otis Taylor.<ref name="Top 10"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=LaMarre |first=Tom |title=Raiders vs. Chiefs amazing history |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/raiders/the-black-hole-plus/las-vegas-raiders-kansas-city-chiefs-derek-carr-patrick-mahomes-nfl |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=Sports Illustrated |date=13 November 2021 |language=en}}</ref> After a bench-clearing brawl, Davidson and Taylor were ejected, and the penalties that were called nullified the first down under the rules at the time. Kansas City was forced to punt. The Raiders took advantage, as [[George Blanda]] made a 48-yard field goal with 8 seconds left to secure a 17–17 tie. The tie proved to be costly for the Chiefs, as Oakland clinched their first AFC West championship with a 20–6 victory in Oakland in Week 13. Due to this incident, the NFL changed the rules so that Davidson's personal foul would have been enforced at the end of the play, and Taylor's penalty would have been assessed only after the Chiefs had been awarded a first down.

The Chiefs defeated the Raiders 42–10 in the [[1975 NFL season|1975 season]], prompting the Chiefs' live [[horse]] [[mascot]] [[Warpaint (horse)|Warpaint]] to circle the field after each touchdown scored. After the game, Raiders coach [[John Madden]] said "We couldn't beat the Chiefs, but we damn near killed their horse." It was the first win for new Chiefs coach [[Paul Wiggin]].<ref name="Chiefs cheerleaders">{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20120210211812/http://www.georgeblowfish.com/Chiefspage7.html Chiefs cheerleaders and mascots]}}, Accessed March 15, 2008.</ref>

The Raiders won two more Super Bowl titles in [[1980 NFL season|1980]]<ref name="1980 Oakland Raiders">{{cite web|url=http://profootballreference.com/teams/rai1980.htm|title=1980 Oakland Raiders Statistics & Players - Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=August 29, 2016|archive-date=March 17, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060317121638/http://www.profootballreference.com/teams/rai1980.htm}}</ref> and [[1983 NFL season|1983]]<ref name="1983 Oakland Raiders">{{cite web|url=http://profootballreference.com/teams/rai1983.htm|title=1983 Los Angeles Raiders Statistics & Players - Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=August 29, 2016|archive-date=April 23, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070423193754/http://www.profootballreference.com/teams/rai1983.htm}}</ref> while the Chiefs were considered to be one of the worst teams in the NFL. The Raiders won most of the games between the 1970s and 1980s.<ref name="The Rivalry">[http://www.chiefswarpath.com/rivalry/rivalry.htm The Rivalry - Kansas City vs. Oakland] ''ChiefsWarpath.com''</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-04 |title=The heated history of Raiders vs. Chiefs rivalry - Vegas Sports Today |url=https://vegassportstoday.com/heated-history-raiders-vs-chiefs-rivarly/ |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=vegassportstoday.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Following their victory in Super Bowl IV, the Chiefs returned to the playoffs in [[1971 NFL season|1971]], but lost in double overtime to the [[Miami Dolphins]] in the divisional round in the longest game in NFL history, the final game at Kansas City's Municipal Stadium. Following that loss, Kansas City did not return to the playoffs until 1986.<ref name="1986 Kansas City Chiefs">{{cite web|url=http://profootballreference.com/teams/kan1986.htm|title=1986 Kansas City Chiefs Statistics & Players - Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=August 29, 2016|archive-date=April 26, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070426012156/http://www.profootballreference.com/teams/kan1986.htm}}</ref>

In the final game of the [[1999 NFL season|1999 season]], the Chiefs and Raiders faced off at [[Kansas City]]. A win for the Chiefs would put them in the playoffs. A game plagued by special teams mistakes for the Chiefs, including three attempted kickoffs that ended up out of bounds by kickoff specialist Jon Baker, helped keep the Raiders in the game and stop the Chiefs from sealing the victory. The game went into overtime and, helped by favorable field position after the third and final kickoff out of bounds, former Chief [[Rich Gannon]] drove the Raiders into Chiefs territory, setting up the game-winning field goal and knocking the Chiefs out of the playoffs, their first win at Arrowhead since 1988.<ref name="Heartbreaker">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000524210918/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?file=/examiner/archive/2000/01/03/SPORTS3589.dtl Raiders die with their boots on] ''SFGate.com'', 3 January 2000.</ref>

[[File:Oakland Raiders 24, Kansas City Chiefs 0, 2002, by Ken Lund.jpg|thumb|300px|right|Kansas City at Oakland, 2002.]]
On October 21, 2007, the Chiefs defeated the Raiders for a record ninth straight victory. On November 25, 2007, the Raiders defeated the Chiefs in Arrowhead for Oakland's first victory over Kansas City since December 23, 2002.

On September 14, 2008, the Raiders defeated the Chiefs 23–8 for the second straight time in Kansas City. Rookie [[Darren McFadden]] compiled 210 rushing yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=280914012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080918034102/http://scores.espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=280914012|archive-date=September 18, 2008|title=Despite firing reports, Kiffin, McFadden lead Raiders over Chiefs|access-date=August 29, 2016}}</ref> On November 30, 2008, the Chiefs defeated the Raiders for the sixth straight time in Oakland.<ref name="Johnson's 2-yard">{{cite web | title=Johnson's 2-yard plunge lifts Chiefs over woeful Raiders | url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=281130013 | archive-url=https://archive.today/20081202135057/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=281130013 |archive-date=December 2, 2008| agency=Associated Press | publisher=ESPN | date=2008-11-30 | access-date=December 1, 2008}}</ref>

On September 20, 2009, the Raiders defeated the Chiefs 13–10, in Kansas City for the third straight time. The Chiefs became one of the few teams to lose to quarterback [[JaMarcus Russell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=290920012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090925040830/http://scores.espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=290920012|archive-date=September 25, 2009|title=McFadden's late TD helps ruin Cassel's debut for Chiefs|access-date=August 29, 2016}}</ref>
On November 15, 2009, the Chiefs defeated the Raiders 16–10 in Oakland Coliseum for the Chiefs' seventh straight victory in Oakland.

On November 7, 2010, the Raiders defeated the Chiefs in OT 23–20 in a match-up that revived the Chiefs–Raiders rivalry. It marked the 99th time these teams have met in the regular season and 102nd overall. On January 2, 2011, the Raiders defeated the Chiefs in Kansas City for the fourth straight time, 31–10, to finish a sweep of the AFC West.

On October 3, 2011, a Raiders fan filed a lawsuit against the Chiefs and two unidentified Chiefs fans, claiming that security did nothing as he was beaten during a brawl at Kansas City in 2009.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.businessinsurance.com/article/20111003/NEWS05/111009987|title=Kansas City Chiefs face lawsuit over stadium brawl - Business Insurance|first=Matt|last=Dunning|work=Business Insurance |access-date=August 29, 2016}}</ref>

The Chiefs broke Oakland's six-game winning streak in Kansas City on October 13, 2013, when they defeated the Raiders, 24–7, in a game where Kansas City set a then world record for the loudest open-air venue at over 137&nbsp;dB.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kuhla|first=Andrew|title=Arrowhead Sets World Record For Loudest Stadium|url=http://arrowheadaddict.com/2013/10/13/arrowhead-sets-world-record-loudest-stadium/|work=Fansided|date=13 October 2013 |access-date=13 October 2013}}</ref>

On November 20, 2014, the Raiders snapped a 16-game losing streak in Oakland against the Chiefs while Kansas City was in a four-game winning streak the week after the Chiefs defeated the defending [[Super Bowl]] champions, the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. The loss ended up costing Kansas City a playoff berth.

In 2015, the Kansas City Chiefs swept the season series between these two teams.

In 2016, both teams were at the top of the AFC for the entire season, with Oakland securing their first winning season and first playoff appearance since 2002. The Chiefs beat Oakland twice, 26–10 in Oakland and in Kansas City 21–13. Both teams ended the regular season with a 12–4 record and with the series sweep, Kansas City won the AFC West and a first round bye while Oakland was relegated to Wild Card status and the fifth seed in the AFC playoffs.

The Chiefs and Raiders met for a Thursday Night match-up on October 19, 2017, in Oakland, with the Chiefs at a 5–1 record and the Raiders at a 2–4 record. The Raiders won the game 31–30 with a touchdown pass at the very end of the game, which followed two Chiefs defensive penalties, also including a scuffle between the two teams that led to Raiders running back [[Marshawn Lynch]] getting ejected.<ref name="t126">{{cite web | last=Rosenthal | first=Gregg | title=Marshawn Lynch facing possible fines, suspension | website=NFL.com | date=2017-10-19 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/marshawn-lynch-facing-possible-fines-suspension-0ap3000000864111 | access-date=2025-02-09}}</ref> The game snapped a four-game losing streak for Oakland in the season, and also a five-game losing streak against the Chiefs in the rivalry.

In Week 5 of the [[2020 NFL season|2020 season]], the rivalry between the two teams was renewed when the 2–2 Raiders went to [[Arrowhead Stadium]] and upset the undefeated Chiefs 40–32, snapping a 5-game losing streak against the Chiefs dating back to 2017. It was the Raiders' first win in Arrowhead since 2012, with [[Derek Carr]] passing for 347 yards and three touchdowns, while [[Patrick Mahomes]] had 340 yards and two touchdowns, but had a costly third-quarter interception that led to a critical Raiders touchdown. It was Mahomes' first loss to the Raiders, and first loss since losing to the [[2019 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] in Week 10 of the 2019 season.

[[File:Chiefs-Raiders 2021 at Arrowhead Stadium.png|thumb|400px|right|Las Vegas at Kansas City, 2021.]]
On November 22, 2020, the two teams met in Las Vegas for the first time on [[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]. With 1:07 left in the game, Derek Carr threw a touchdown pass to [[Jason Witten]] to give the Raiders a 31–28 lead, but Patrick Mahomes lead a 75-yard drive culminating in a 23-yard touchdown pass to [[Travis Kelce]] with 28 seconds left that gave the Chiefs a 35–31 win, officially renewing a spark in the rivalry between the two teams. After, the Chiefs went on to finish the season 14–2, losing to the [[2020 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Buccaneers]] in [[Super Bowl LV]], while the Raiders, who were 6–3 leading up to this game, began a painful late-season collapse, as they would lose four of their last six games to end the season 8–8 and out of the playoffs.

On Christmas Day 2023, the Raiders defense helped snap another 5-game losing streak against the Chiefs.
